theme: The vision of God’s throne, glory above the exile
readingInstruction: Read Ezekiel 1:1-3:27. A priest in exile by a canal in Babylon sees a vision of God’s throne, eats a scroll, and is made a watchman. Read chapter 1 as a picture rather than a puzzle, and ask what it tells Ezekiel about where God is.
settingTheScene: Ezekiel was a priest, taken to Babylon with the first group of exiles in 597 BC, together with King Jehoiachin. In the fifth year of that exile, at the age of thirty, the age when priests began their service, he saw the vision. He had no temple to serve in, but God came to him by the river Chebar in a foreign land. Ezekiel prophesied for about twenty-two years, and his book is full of visions and sign-acts.
observation: “The heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God” (1:1).
“Out of the midst of it came the likeness of four living creatures” (1:5).
“And above the expanse over their heads there was the likeness of a throne, in appearance like sapphire” (1:26).
“Such was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell on my face” (1:28).
“Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you” (2:1).
“And whether they hear or refuse to hear… they will know that a prophet has been among them” (2:5).
“Son of man, eat whatever you find here. Eat this scroll… and it was in my mouth as sweet as honey” (3:1, 3).
“Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel” (3:17).
interpretation:
Ezekiel’s first vision is overwhelming, and all details point to one great truth: God is on his throne, and he is not confined to Jerusalem. A great storm cloud comes from the north, with flashing fire. Within it are four living creatures with faces of a man, a lion, an ox, and an eagle. Beside each is a wheel within a wheel, full of eyes, moving in every direction. Above is an expanse like crystal, and above that a throne with a figure like a man, surrounded by a rainbow. It is the glory of the LORD.

The point of the vision is clear to anyone who knows the situation. The exiles thought God had stayed in the temple in Jerusalem. They were in a foreign land, far from his presence. But God’s throne is mobile. It comes to Babylon. He is not limited to one place. The wheels move in any direction. He is sovereign over the whole earth.

Ezekiel falls on his face. God calls him “son of man,” a title used about ninety times in the book, emphasizing his humble humanity. He is raised by the Spirit and sent to a people who are “rebellious,” “hard of heart” and “stubborn.” The prophet is warned that they will not listen. His job is to speak, whether they hear or not.

Then he eats a scroll with words of lament, mourning, and woe, and it tastes sweet as honey. The word of God is sweet even when its message is bitter. In the Bible, to eat the word is to take it fully in before speaking it.

At the end of chapter 3, God makes him a watchman. If he warns, and they do not listen, he has saved himself. If he does not warn, he will be held accountable. The prophet is given seven days of silence, overwhelmed by the task. And then God binds his tongue, so that he speaks only when God gives him a word.
connection: Revelation 4:6-8 shows four living creatures around the throne, and Revelation 1:12-18 shows the glorified Christ. John 1:14 says the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, “and we have seen his glory.” Matthew 28:19-20 sends the disciples into all the world and promises his presence. Revelation 10:8-11 shows John eating a scroll, as Ezekiel did. Acts 20:26-31 shows Paul acting as a watchman, innocent of the blood of all.
application:
Pause and remember that God is not confined to the places you associate with him. Pray to him wherever you are today.

Eat the word: take a short passage and read it slowly until you taste it.

Think about whom God has made you a watchman for: family, friends, a church. How are you warning and encouraging them?
prayerPrompts: Praise God for being seated on his throne.
Thank him that he came to the exiles in Babylon, and to you.
Ask him to give you ears to hear his word.
